query: interfaces in src that a For the class-matched detections in one capture, select_stage2_subset ranks that DetectionCandidate list with the strategy select_detection already implements. It applies that strategy by the first-maximum rule std::max_element already uses, so a tie keeps the earlier candidate and the later tied candidate stays deferred. It admits at most the count the caller passes, in that rank order, and places every candidate it does not admit into deferred, preserving their order in the candidate list. Each candidate keeps its source_index. Stage2Admission holds those two vectors, admitted and deferred. An empty candidate list returns both vectors empty, and an unknown strategy throws. The pose node calls it with its detection_selection strategy and a count of one, so stage 2 still estimates that single admitted pallet. The admitted source index and the deferred source indices are written on PalletPoseStamped after input_depth_stamp. The message already carries this pair's RGB and depth stamps, so the split is this capture while the scene can still change. When the estimate fails, publish no PalletPoseStamped and write the same two lists on the failure diagnostic, which is the only result that path publishes. The two early returns that publish nothing stay as they are. The user named which detections are sent through stage 2 versus marked deferred. The part they did not name is that the split is these two admission vectors, ordered by that first-maximum rule, on the pose result the handling process reads. change must keep working
findings: select_stage2_subset has to rank with the same two strategies select_detection already implements, and with the same first-maximum rule. highest_confidence orders by score then area_px; largest_area orders by area_px then score. source_index is not a key. std::max_element returns the iterator to the first greatest element, and its reference implementation updates the leader only when the comparator says the current leader is less than the next element, so an equal pair keeps the earlier DetectionCandidate and the later tied candidate stays deferred. std::sort does not preserve the order of equivalent elements, so a sort-then-truncate ranking can admit the later tie and defer the earlier one. The recorder mirror select_best_detection uses Python max with key (score, area) or (area, score), and max returns the first maximal item, the same first-maximum rule as sorted(..., reverse=True)[0]. A count of one must therefore admit the same candidate select_detection returns, which is the bbox the recorder stores. Admitted candidates are that rank order, length at most the count the caller passes. Every candidate not admitted goes into deferred in its original candidate-list order, not in rank order and not renumbered. Each DetectionCandidate in both vectors keeps its source_index. Stage2Admission is those two vectors. An empty candidate list returns both vectors empty and does not throw. Any strategy other than the two named ones throws std::invalid_argument, which is what select_detection throws today and what the node does not catch. The pose node calls this with its detection_selection parameter and a count of one. geometry_core::estimate_pose_chamfer_v3_2 still runs once, on that single admitted bbox, with that source_index as instance_id. Deferred candidates are not estimated.

The pose result the handling process reads is pps_perception_msgs/PalletPoseStamped on pallet_pose_topic (default and pallet_pose_cpp.yaml /pps/pallet_pose_rich, publisher depth 10). The message comment names this rich pose as the AGV controller result. eval_recorder_node is the only subscriber in src. It joins format_stamp(input_rgb_stamp) to stamp_map.json and copies yaw_rad, pose.position, n_face_points, plane_inlier_ratio, and chamfer_cost_m. It does not read a source index today. Existing fields stay in place and stay filled on the success publish: header.stamp is the node clock and header.frame_id is the detection frame or camera_rgb_optical_frame; pose is the optical-frame yaw quaternion; yaw_rad, face_normal_rgb, plane_inlier_ratio, n_face_points, chamfer_cost_m (0 when has_debug is false), accepted true, failure_reason empty, geometry_source, preset_id geometry_core_default, input_rgb_stamp, and input_depth_stamp. quality_reasons stays the default empty string array and is not the deferred list. ROS 2 IDL field order is the order written in the msg. int32 is int32_t and int32[] is an unbounded sequence; names are lowercase and must not collide with the fields already there. The admitted source index and the deferred source indices append after input_depth_stamp, which is the last field. With the node count of one, that is one int32 for the admitted source_index and one int32[] for the deferred source_index values in candidate-list order. A zero admitted index is a real detections slot, because a default int32 is 0 and extract locks source_index 0. An empty deferred sequence is the one class-matched candidate. The four srv files generated beside this msg do not reference it. geometry_msgs/PoseStamped on pose_topic (yaml and the mock pipeline /pps/pallet_pose) stays a header plus a pose. test_full_pipeline_launch.py requires a finite pose with tz in (1.5, 2.5) and |tx| and |ty| under 0.20 m, which is this single admitted pallet. dataset_replay.launch maps its pose_topic argument (default /pps/pallet_pose_rich) onto pallet_pose_topic and the recorder, and leaves the node pose_topic parameter on the yaml PoseStamped name.

DetectionCandidate.source_index is the index in vision_msgs/Detection2DArray.detections. extract_detection_candidates walks that array in order, skips an empty results list and a target_class_id mismatch, and does not renumber, which test_detection_utils locks (empty results yield no candidate; a forklift at slot 0 leaves the pallet at source_index 1). The class compared is the highest-scoring ObjectHypothesis.class_id string. The detector writes class_label (pallet), not the numeric pallet_class_id, into that string, copies the RGB Image header onto the array, leaves Detection2D.id empty, and publishes score-descending boxes capped by max_detections (default 10). Detection2D.id is the optional cross-message id and may be empty, so the roster slots are the stored source_index values, not id. Class mismatches are absent from both admission vectors. Candidate-list order is increasing source_index order of the class-matched detections, so the earlier tie is the lower source_index and the later tie stays deferred. target_class_id pallet and detection_selection highest_confidence stay aligned in pallet_pose_cpp.yaml, pipeline_nodes.py, and dataset_replay.launch.py. select_detection itself stays: nullopt on an empty list, the first maximum otherwise, and std::invalid_argument on an unknown strategy. PoseResult.instance_id and FailureResult.instance_id hold the optional int passed into the one estimate and are not a published field today.

The pair interface is message_filters ApproximateTime of sensor_msgs/Image and Detection2DArray, queue sync_queue_size 10, setMaxIntervalDuration from sync_slop_s (default 0.10 s). Topics stay the parameters (yaml depth /camera/depth/image_rect, detections /pps/detections). input_rgb_stamp is det_msg->header.stamp. input_depth_stamp is depth_msg->header.stamp. PalletPoseStamped already carries both as builtin_interfaces/Time, whose nanosec is in [0, 1e9). The Image header timestamp is the acquisition time, and Detection2D says the source pixels are not in the message and the header should match that source, recovered with an approximate synchronizer. The two capture stamps can differ inside the slop. Diagnostics carry stamp_to_string, seconds, a dot, and nanosec zero-padded to 9, the same text as build_bag.format_stamp. The recorder joins both the rich pose and the WARN diagnostic on that input_rgb_stamp text. DiagnosticArray.header.stamp and both pose headers stay publish time. The new index fields ride on the same PalletPoseStamped as those two capture stamps, so the admission split is this pair while the scene can still change.

A stage-2 failure publishes one diagnostic_msgs/DiagnosticArray and returns. That is the only result on that path: no geometry_msgs/PoseStamped and no PalletPoseStamped. The status stays name pps_pallet_pose_cpp, hardware_id dynamic_handling_ros_v1, level WARN (1), message equal to failure_reason, with KeyValues failure_reason, input_rgb_stamp, and input_depth_stamp. KeyValue is a string key and a string value, so the admitted source index and the deferred source indices are two further string values on keys that are not those three. The recorder builds a dict and keeps the last value for a repeated key, joins on input_rgb_stamp, and stores failure_reason or else status.message. A later WARN with the same stamp replaces that diag. _build_record uses the rich pose whenever it arrived, so a PalletPoseStamped on the failure path would take the success branch and hide the failure. The two lists are appended on this same WARN, and they leave failure_reason, input_rgb_stamp, and input_depth_stamp in place. The success OK status stays message pose_estimated with chamfer_cost_m, plane_inlier_ratio, n_face_points, and both stamps. The recorder skips every DiagnosticStatus whose level is not WARN, so the success-path lists have to be on PalletPoseStamped.

The two early returns stay unpublished. An empty candidate list, which is an empty Stage2Admission, returns before depth conversion and before stage 2. depth_image_to_meters throws std::invalid_argument on an unsupported encoding or a short buffer, and that path only logs. The recorder marks a sample with neither a rich pose nor a WARN diagnostic as no_response, and a WARN as failed. A diagnostic on either early return would record a failure for a pair that currently records no_response. An unknown detection_selection still throws out of the callback rather than becoming a diagnostic. mock pipeline_nodes sets pose_topic and pallet_pose_topic and omits diagnostics_topic, so the C++ default /pps/pallet_pose_diagnostics must stay that name. Publishers use depth 10, which is keep-last on rmw_qos_profile_default: reliable and volatile. The recorder subscription is reliable, volatile, depth 50. A best-effort publisher would not match that subscription. Keep-last drops whole messages, so one PalletPoseStamped carries both index lists and both capture stamps, and the failure path carries both lists on its one WARN.
